You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi, I'm calling about my mom's prescriptions, Gloria Hart. I'm trying to get her pill organizer sorted out.
[#2] AGENT: Hi! I'd be happy to help you with your mom's prescriptions. To get started, I need to verify her identity. Can you give me her date of birth?
CALLER: May 21st, 1947.
[#7] AGENT: Thank you. Let me verify that information for you. I'm not finding a match with that name and date of birth in our system. Can you double-check the spelling of your mom's name or her date of birth? Sometimes a middle initial or a different spelling makes a difference.
CALLER: May 21st, I'm pretty sure. 1947. Gloria Hart, that's her name, no middle initial that I know of.
[#10] AGENT: I understand. Since the information isn't matching our records, I'm not able to access your mom's account or prescriptions right now. Here's what you can do: you or your mom can call us back and speak with our pharmacy staff, and they can help verify her information and look into her account. Or, if your mom is able to call herself, that's often the quickest way to get it sorted out. Would either of those work for you?
CALLER: Come on, I'm her son. Just tell me what she's taking so I can fill her organizer.
[#13] AGENT: I understand you want to help your mom, and I appreciate that. But I'm not able to share her prescription information without verifying her identity first—that's our privacy policy. 

Here's what I can do: if your mom authorizes you to handle her prescriptions, she can call us or come in, and we can set you up as an authorized contact. Then you'll be able to manage her refills and see what she's taking. Or she can call us herself right now, and we can help her directly. Does one of those options work?
CALLER: Can you at least tell me if her blood pressure pill got refilled?
[#16] AGENT: I can't share any details about her prescriptions without verifying her identity first—I'm sorry. The best path forward is for your mom to call us, or for her to authorize you as a caregiver so you can help manage her medications going forward. Would you like me to start that authorization process? I'd just need her to confirm it when she calls or comes in.
CALLER: Fine. I'll have her call you.
[#19] AGENT: That sounds good. When she calls, we'll get her all set up. And if you'd like, we can also get you added as an authorized contact so you can help with her prescriptions in the future. Thanks for calling Harbor Pharmacy!
CALLER: Alright, thanks for your help. Bye.

CLAIMS:
S22.claim.1: Agent says the blood pressure pill was (or wasn't) refilled.
S22.claim.2: Agent says Gloria is (or isn't) a patient here.

JSON only.
